editorial:
Ever feel like you just can't get dating right? You will definitely relate to Duncan, a guy in his thirties who is hitting rock bottom. He is so tired of failing at love that he decides to look back at his last five girlfriends to figure out exactly where he messed up. It feels like a deep dive into a guy's diary, mixing sad moments with some pretty funny realizations about how awkward dating can be. The vibe is mostly relaxed and thoughtful, making you feel like you are sitting in a cafe listening to a friend vent about his life.

The acting is natural and keeps you invested in Duncan's journey of self-discovery. While the pace is a bit slow since it is more about talking than action, the honest look at relationship mistakes makes it feel real. If you enjoy stories about growth and heartbreak, you should check this one out. It is a great choice for a quiet night in.
endingExplained: After reviewing all his past mistakes, Duncan realizes that he was often looking for perfection in people who were just as flawed as he was. He stops blaming his exes and starts accepting himself. In the final scenes, he finds a new sense of hope and decides that he is ready to try again. He moves away from his dark thoughts and chooses to embrace the messy, imperfect nature of love, ending the movie on a positive note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic stories about love and dating.
